html:
A significant diplomatic rift has emerged between Israel and a coalition of Western nations, led by the UK, over Israeli settlements, while a major trade dispute has intensified between the United States and Canada, signaling deepening fragmentation in global alliances.

Great Power Dynamics: Canada has dramatically escalated its trade dispute with the US, imposing tariffs as high as 50% on nearly $20 billion of US products, from steel to T-shirts, with Carney noting the US trade war "will come at a cost." This move follows US President Donald Trump's threats against Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier and comes amidst Democratic accusations that Trump's proposal to rename New Mexico to 'New America' is a distraction from an unpopular Iran war and persistent inflation. Elsewhere, Hungary's expulsion of 10 Russian diplomats has drawn a "harsh and painful" response from Moscow, which views it as part of a "Russophobic lobby."

Israel and Regional Conflict: The UK, France, Canada, Sweden, and nine other European countries have moved to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accusing the Israeli government of turning a "blind eye" to "ethnic cleansing" by settlers. In retaliation, Israel will close the UK consulate in Jerusalem and plans further measures against Britain, including expelling UK representatives from a headquarters in Kiryat Gat. Meanwhile, a Palestinian child was killed in Gaza and Israeli strikes killed at least 27 people and destroyed a hospital in southern Lebanon. An Israeli court rejected a petition to halt a key West Bank settlement project.

Ukraine War and Russia: In Ukraine, five people were killed when a Russian drone strike hit the We Are Ukraine TV channel building during a live broadcast in Kyiv, President Zelensky said. Despite this, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov expressed Russia's confidence that victory in its war against Ukraine is "very near." Simultaneously, Ukraine is developing its own ballistic missile, designed by a "millennial woman," which is expected to put Moscow within reach. Lithuania is also training civilians for defense amid fears of Russia's war spreading.

Middle East Security and Energy: Tensions remain high in the Middle East as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian cities and energy facilities injured 73 people and caused fires, prompting Saudi Arabia to vow a firm response to what it calls a dangerous escalation. The World Food Programme highlights a severe food insecurity crisis in Yemen. Concurrently, Iran's Acting Defense Minister stated Iran is capable of targeting US warships enforcing economic blockades, with Iran also announcing plans for a new 'exclusion zone' near the Strait of Hormuz. The IAEA revealed a secret Assad-era Syrian nuclear reactor was almost complete and configured for nuclear weapons.

Global Concerns and Domestic Shifts: Sudan's healthcare system is reportedly on the brink of collapse, with Médecins Sans Frontières urging world leaders to increase funding for millions needing aid. In Europe, protests against the far-right AfD are sweeping Germany as the party targets gains in two more states, raising questions for Merz's government. Adding to regional tensions, the funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, was condemned as "shocking" by Ursula von der Leyen and could influence upcoming elections.
